paragraphs.text: I. QUESTION WORDS IN TAGALOG There are 14 different question words in the tagalog language that correspond to the English question words who, what, which, how, why, when, where and whose. These are:

slides.title: The word "Sino" in Tagalog is an interrogative pronoun used to ask "Who?“

paragraphs.text: SINO								WHO
Example:
Sino ba kayo ? Who are you?
Sino ang kumain ng tinapay ? 		Who ate the bread?
‘Ano " is an interrogative pronoun in Tagalog that means "What " in English. It is used to ask about things, ideas, events, or situations — essentially anything that is not a person.
ANO WHAT example:
Ano ba ang pangalan ninyo ? What is your name?
Ano ito ? 												What is this?
Ano ang pangalan mo ?								What is your name?
Ano ang ginagawa mo ?								What are you doing?

Alin " is another interrogative pronoun, and in English, it means "which". Is used when choosing one or more items from a known group or set. It asks for specific identification within that group. ALIN							WHICH example: halimbawa Alin ba ang iyong gusto?				Which do you like? Alin sa mga ito ang sa iyo ?			Which of these is yours? Alin ang mas mabigat : bakal o tingga ?		Which is heavier: iron or lead?
GAANO is a tagalog interrogative word used to ask about extent , degree , or measurement —
GAANO								HOW
example: halimbawa
Gaano ka laki ang Pilipinas?			How large is the Philippines? ( requires a response expressing degree or quality )
Gaano ka tagal ?						How long?
Gaano ka laki ang bahay mo ?			How big is your house?
Gaano + [ka- + adjective/adverb]					" Gaano " – asks about degree/ exten "Ilan" – asks how many (quantity)
ka- is a prefix that links " Gaano " to a descriptive word
Long- Mahaba
Long- time frame ------ Matagal
PAANO is a Tagalog interrogative word that means "How" — specifically used to ask about the manner, method, or process by which something is done.
PAANO 									HOW
Example: halimbawa Paano mo malalaman ?				How will you know ? (requires a response detailing a process)
Paano ka natutong magluto ?			How did you learn to cook?
Paano mo nalaman ?					How did you know?
Tip: Usually followed by a verb or verb phrase
Can be used in questions about instructions, explanations, or procedures
Bakit" is an interrogative word in Tagalog that means "Why" in English. It is used to ask for reasons , causes , or explanations behind an action, situation, or event .
BAKIT											WHY
example: halimbawa
Bakit siya galit ?								Why is he/she angry?
Bakit ka umalis ?							Why did you leave?
Bakit hindi siya dumating ?				Why didn’t he/she come?
Tip: Usually followed by a subject + verb or a verb + subject construction.
Can appear at the beginning of the sentence or before the reason clause.
"Kailan" is a Tagalog interrogative word that means "When " in English. It is used to ask about time — whether past, present, or future .
KAILAN											WHEN
Example: halimbawa
Kailan kayo dumating sa Pilipinas?			When did you arrive in the Philippines?
Kailan tayo aalis ?								When are we leaving?
Kailan mo siya nakilala ? When did you meet him/her?
Usually placed at the beginning of the sentence
Often followed by a verb or subject + verb
" Nasaan " is used when the subject is specific or known (often a proper noun or identified item).It is usually followed by a proper noun or a definite noun (e.g., si Nanay, ang libro , ang aso ).
“NASAAN " is an interrogative word in Tagalog used to ask about the location or position of a person, thing, or place . In English, it means "Where is..." or simply "Where?“
NASAAN						WHERE
Nasaan siya ?				Where is he/she?(when asking for the location of a 										person or thing)
Nasaan ang bag mo ? Where is your bag?
Nasaan na tayo?	 		Where are we now?
Nasaan ang susi ?			Where is the key?

"Saan" functions as an interrogative adverb — it's used to ask about location or direction , and it typically translates to "where" in english .’ SAAN					WHERE example: halimbawa Saan kayo nakatira ?		Where do you live? Saan ang ospital ? 			Where is the hospital? Saan siya galing ?			Where did he/she come from? Saan tayo kakain ?			Where we eat?
malaman = to know					gusto = to like
nakatira = live/reside simbahan = church
galit = angry dumating = arrived
tao = person pelikula = movie

"ILAN " is an interrogative pronoun/adjective that means " how many” ILAN 					HOW MANY example: halimbawa Ilan ang anak ninyo / mo ? 		How many children do you have? Ilan sila sa klase ?			How many are they in the class? Ilan kayo sa pamilya ?		How many are you in the family?

“MAGKANO" is an interrogative word that means "how much" — usually used when asking about price or cost. Magkano How much Example : halimbawa Magkano ang aklat ? 		How much is the book? Magkano ang sapatos ?		How much are the shoes? Magkano ang kinita mo ?		How much did you earn? Magkano ang pamasahe ?	 	How much is the fare

"KANINO " Is an interrogative pronoun that means " to whom" or "whose ", depending on the context. KANINO						WHOSE Kanino ang bahay na iyan ? 			Whose house is that? Kanino ang cellphone?				Whose cellphone is it? Kanino ka nagsabi ?				To whom did you say it? Questions beginning with kanino require responses that point to akin (mine), kaniya (his or her), kanila (their) or other possessive pronouns. Para sa kanino For whom para sa kanino iyan ? For whom is that? Sa kanino with/to whom sa kanino iyan ? To whom does that belong?

slides.title: II. THE PLURAL FORMS OF QUESTION WORDS

paragraphs.text: In Prev.lesson, the pluralization of either or both the predicate and subject of a sentence has been pointed out. Plural markers such as sina , nina , ng mga and ang mga have also been introduced.
Question words are not exempt from the plurality rule either.
The plural forms of these interrogatives are formed by duplicating the question words or certain syllables of the question words based on the following rules:

slides.title: I.	When a word is composed of two syllables , the whole word is duplicated :

paragraphs.text: alin becomes alin-alin
sino becomes sinu-sino
II. When a word has three or more syllables , only the first two syllables are duplicated:
kanino becomes kani-kanino
magkano becomes magka-magkano
III.The o in the last syllable becomes u in the first half of the new duplicated word.
ano becomes anu- ano sino becomes sinu-sino
The plural forms of these interrogative words are used when more than one thing is being referred to and when an answer in the plural form is expected.

The interrogatives nasaan and bakit are never duplicated for the simple reason that nothing or no one can be in more than one place at the same time nor can there be more than one explanation for an event or action.
The following are examples of questions using duplicated interrogatives.
Sinu- sino ang inyong mga anak ? Which of the children are yours?
Anu- ano ang mga pangalan ninyo ? What are your names?
Kani- kanino ang mga bahay na iyan ? Whose houses are those?
Saan- saan kayo nakatira ? Where do you (plural) live?
Magka-magkano ang mga aklat ? How much are each of the books?
llan-llan ang mga anak nila ? How many children do they have?

In the ilan-ilan question above, the speaker is referring to the total number of children of more than one couple or parent. The question may be translated to Between those two (or three) couples (or parents), how many children do they have in all?
Kai-kailan kayo dumating sa Pilipinas ?
When (plural, referring to several dates) did you (plural) arrive in the Philippines?
Note that kai-kailan is very infrequently used nowadays and is mostly confined in rural Tagalog areas or regions.

Contracted and shortened forms of a word or two words together are very common in spoken Tagalog, as in English. In the case of interrogatives, ligatures may produce another version of a question. Both iyan and ito may also be shortened to ' yan and 'to . They lose the stresses on the second syllable as both become monosyllabic modifiers. Note the differences in the following Tagalog questions.
Sino ang taong iyan ?		 	Who is that person?
Sinong tao iyan ?				Who is that (person
Sino ' yan ?				(Speaker is pointing to someone)

slides.title: Kanino ang aklat na ito ? 			Whose book is this?

paragraphs.text: Kanino ng aklat Ito?				Whose (book) is this?
Kanino ‘to? (Speaker is pointing to or holding a book)
Ano ang simbahang iyan ? 			What church is that?
Anong simbahan iyan ?			What (church) is that?
Ano ' yan ? (Speaker is pointing to a church)

Other common questions aside from the ones mentioned above that need to be committed to mem­ory are the following. Note the presence of ba (the use of ba is discussed in the next lesson) in these questions.
Kilala mo ba siya ? 				 			Do you know her/him?
Sasama ka ba ?								 Are you coming along?
Gusto mo ba ito ? 							Do you like this?
Uuwi ka na ba ?					 			Are you going home already?
Gusto mo bang manood ng sine?				Do you like to watch a movie?
Tama ba ito ?									Is this correct?
Tama ba ako ?								 Am I right?
Ano ba ' yan ?				 				What's that?
Anong gusto mo ?			 				What do you like?
Saan ka pupunta ?			 				Where are you going?
Sino ba siya ? 				 				Who's she/he?
Nasaan siya ?								 Where's she/he?
